findings.why: The repeated dashes and repeated return to “came” made me hold the main action open through several layers of description.
I had to slow down to understand the distinction between what her body knew how to do and what she was now actually doing.
The long fragment accumulates direction, repetition, and comparison before its shape becomes clear.
I had to stop and mentally assemble the bench’s geometry from the peak, the two downward angles, and the pivoting leg rests.
I reread “felt the first of her gathered at the seam” because I could not immediately tell what “the first of her” referred to.
The sentence carries many body parts, supports, movements, and interruptions in one chain; I had to reread it to reconstruct her final position.
The phrase “the precision of the thing he had made it to have” took real work to parse.
The opening quotation from the previous sentence never closes, so I initially read the narration here as part of her speech and had to back up.
The path of his hand, the physical details, and the nested sensory descriptions all arrive in one long movement that took concentration to track.
The preceding quotation is left open, making this narration look like continued dialogue until the sentence is reinterpreted.
The repeated uses of “cry,” “sound,” “hear,” and “again” made me work to keep straight what she did, what he perceived, and what he then chose to repeat.
I stumbled over “her face which was at the low point” and had to reorient the spatial description before continuing.
The quotation beginning in the previous sentence is not closed before this narration, so I had to reread to separate his spoken words from his action.
The repeated “that was not” clauses delayed the sentence’s destination long enough that I had to keep several abstractions suspended at once.
The sentence moves through her attempted expression, its reflection, her interpretation, tears, and a remembered sound without a stopping point; I had to slow down to preserve the sequence.
The sentence combines several abstract reversals about aliveness, terror, agency, and bodily action, and I had to unpack them one at a time.
I had to track the distinction among the face, the self, what could be given away, and what incurred a cost across a long chain of clauses.
The uninterrupted sequence carries her movement, appearance, his reaction, and two possible questions in one sentence, so the main action took effort to hold onto.
The sentence shifts from the apple to appetite, self-denial, and being fed through several embedded phrases; I had to slow down to follow the metaphorical turn.
The many future actions and repeated conjunctions made me hold a long sequence in mind before the sentence reached its final point.
